what it is: the NEAR account id. it is the PRIMARY KEY because an account has exactly one api key, ever
the api key. stored as it is — the key is ours and the db is ours, and the key has to be producible again on a later sign-in
the sha-256 of the key. a request is looked up by this, so the read path never compares against every row's key
when the key was created in ms since the epoch
when the key was last touched in ms since the epoch
the uuid v4 that names the batch. it is the PRIMARY KEY and it is what goes in the url
what the transactions do in words. null says there was no what
when they should happen in words. the column is quoted because `when` is a reserved word in sqlite
why the user wants them
the machine-readable version of `when` in epoch ms. null when there is no moment
when the batch was queued in ms since the epoch
when the batch was last touched in ms since the epoch
the uuid v4 that names one transaction inside the batch. it is the PRIMARY KEY. a uuid and not queue_id + position, because the position is renumbered when a call is removed from the middle
the batch this transaction belongs to. a FOREIGN KEY to tx_queue(queue_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
the order of this transaction inside the batch from zero. it is what the wallet popup needs
the contract being called. it has its own column so the stats query is a GROUP BY and not a json scan
the method name. it has its own column for the same reason as contract_id
the arguments as a compact json object held as a string. it stays a json column because it is a bag of arbitrary keys with no shape
the gas as a string. null when the call has no gas of its own
the deposit as a string. null when the call has no deposit of its own
when the transaction was queued in ms since the epoch
when the transaction was last touched in ms since the epoch
the batch the transaction belongs to. it is kept as a column even though it is not part of the primary key, so "every account on this queue" is one indexed read
the transaction the account is on. part of the PRIMARY KEY (tx_id, account_id) and a FOREIGN KEY to tx_queue_transactions(tx_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
the account. part of the PRIMARY KEY (tx_id, account_id)
where the account is with this transaction: pending / sent / succeeded / failed. the ONLY place a status lives — there is none on tx_queue and none on tx_queue_transactions
the hash of the transaction the account sent. null until somebody sends. a row with a hash is history and is never deleted
when the row was created in ms since the epoch
when the row was last touched in ms since the epoch
